findings_detail.description: onConnect() claims the redirect ticket by peer address alone (ClaimRedirect matches m_address). Any TCP connection from that IP to the stream-1 port, before any authentication, consumes the in-flight ticket. The later CMSG_AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION payload is never verified (HandlePacket returns true without checking the digest), so the address is the only binding.

findings_detail.description: SendResumeComms() is sent before PromoteToSlotOne(). If promotion then fails (session gone or redirect superseded), the client has already been told this socket is its second stream while the server drops it and refuses the redirect.

findings_detail.description: In Verifier, when the stored password hash decodes to more than DigestWidth (20) bytes, the condition at line 67 is false and the digest buffer stays all zeros. The function then hashes a zero digest and returns a verifier with no error. A corrupted or malformed account row silently yields a verifier that no client password can match.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Reject hashes longer than DigestWidth (return a failure or throw) instead of silently hashing an all-zero digest.

findings_detail.description: The SRP width constants are defined twice: SRP_EPHEMERAL_WIDTH, SRP_SESSION_KEY_WIDTH, SRP_GENERATOR_WIDTH and SRP_RECONNECT_WIDTH here, and again as Srp6::EphemeralWidth and related names in Srp6.h. AuthSocket also keeps s_BYTE_SIZE for the salt width. SRP_SESSION_KEY_WIDTH is no longer used in this file after the move to Srp6, so it is dead code and a second source of truth that can drift.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Delete the local SRP_* constants and use the Srp6:: constants everywhere, including the salt width instead of s_BYTE_SIZE.

findings_detail.description: The client proof is compared with memcmp on line 771, and the reconnect proof on line 989, so the comparison time depends on how many leading bytes match. The same non-constant-time comparison is used for the reconnect proof. The attacker's timing signal is weak, but a fixed-time comparison is the standard for authentication tags.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Compare M1 and R2 with a constant-time comparison such as CRYPTO_memcmp or a hand-written XOR-accumulate loop.

findings_detail.description: The golden vectors are generated by the same Srp6 and BigNumber code they are meant to check (CryptoGoldenCapture.cpp calls Srp6::Verifier, ServerEphemeral, SessionKey and the proof functions and prints the results). The tests therefore only detect changes from the captured state. A wrong formula, such as a mistake in the interleaved SessionKey hashing or the proof input order, would be captured as correct and never flagged. No independent reference from a real 4.3.4 client or a published SRP-6a test vector is used.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Derive at least one handshake from an independent source (a recorded 4.3.4 client login or a published SRP-6a reference vector) and assert the Srp6 output against it.

findings_detail.description: Return values from EVP_PKEY_sign_init, EVP_PKEY_encrypt_init, EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_rsa_padding, EVP_RSA_gen and BN_MONT_CTX_set are not checked. If any call fails, the harness writes uninitialised or stale timing numbers and golden output with no error.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Check each OpenSSL return value and exit with a message on failure before printing results.

findings_detail.description: The width guard is a substring search for the literal text "AsByteArray()" and two other strings. It does not check whether any width is derived from a value. A call written with different spacing or a different helper bypasses it, while an unrelated occurrence would fail the build, so the guard catches the wrong things in both directions.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Replace the text searches with a check that every AsByteArray call in the SRP6 path passes a named width constant.
